trajectory_summary: This is a short, cooperative call where the customer pre-qualifies himself (buying a home, planning a new roof, wants solar after) and the entire conversation becomes a scheduling puzzle around his home closing and travel dates. The rep never runs verify, roof, utility, bill, or any qualification beats — she solves the calendar problem and ends with a promise to call back on the 4th to actually set the appointment. Energy stayed positive throughout, but structurally nothing was locked and no qualification data was captured, leaving this as a fragile callback rather than a real booking.
outcome_dispute: This should not be tagged as booked/tentative in the sense of a locked appointment — no day or time was set for the actual solar consultation; the rep only promised to call back on the 4th to schedule it. The correct read is 'callback,' and even that is contingent on the home purchase closing, per the customer's own words 'I would call you if something went sideways and it didn't close.'

observed_outcome.quote: K. What if I give you a call on the fourth? Then we can set up an appointment for somebody to be there either the sixth or the seventh.
observed_outcome.reasoning: No specific day/time was locked for the actual solar consultation — the rep committed only to calling the customer back on the 4th to then schedule an appointment for the 6th or 7th, and the entire plan is contingent on the home purchase closing per the customer's own words.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: No bill or usage figure was ever discussed — the customer doesn't yet own the property, and the rep never asked about utility company or expected usage even in general terms.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Mhmm. And I'm gonna put a a new roof on it, and then I wanna put solar on it.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked what interested the customer in solar, but the customer volunteered his reason (new roof, then solar) unprompted; the rep never circled back to reinforce or route this reason, notably missing the roofing cross-sell tie-in.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: And I'm gonna put a a new roof on it, and then I wanna put solar on it.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer handed the rep the exact roof-replacement-planned trigger in the first 30 seconds and the rep never mentioned Ion's in-house roofing — a clean revenue miss that costs nothing to catch and the schema flags as high-value (cross_sell_signals.roof_replacement_planned).

key_moments.quote: So this is Holland with Ion. I got a a request that you were looking into solar for your home.
key_moments.stewart_read: The intro names the company but skips state, referral-source specificity, or any credibility anchor beyond 'I got a request.' It works here only because the customer was already primed and warm, not because the intro did the legitimacy work.

key_moments.quote: So I was thinking if if I could schedule somebody tentatively, fifth through twelfth, but, you know, and I would call you if something went sideways and it didn't close.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer explicitly conditions the entire appointment on his home purchase closing — this is the load-bearing sentence for why the outcome is fragile, not the later scheduling-mechanics exchange.

key_moments.quote: but at least I'll have keys by the fifth is what I would think.
key_moments.stewart_read: A second explicit hedge ('is what I would think') on the timeline reinforces that nothing here is locked — the whole plan rests on assumptions about the closing date holding.

key_moments.quote: K. What if I give you a call on the fourth? Then we can set up an appointment for somebody to be there either the sixth or the seventh.
key_moments.stewart_read: The call resolves into a promise for a future callback to schedule, not a locked appointment day/time. There is no 'is that fair?' handshake, no hour-block statement, no confirmation mechanics — this is a plan to make a plan, not a booked appointment.
